newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela mulls whether to forego IMF loan tranche.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela mulls whether to forego IMF loan tranche.

text.p: Venezuela's government is mulling whether to forego a second tranche of a $1.4 billion IMF standby loan, a senior Venezuelan official said Monday.

"We are discussing whether we really need that disbursement, now that our foreign reserves have risen so much. We have dollars coming out of our ears," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"But even if we decided to pass on the second tranche, we would still meet the targets agreed with the IMF," he added.
Venezuela reached an agreement in principle with the International Monetary Fund in April to support its fiscal adjustment program.
Among the goals they agreed was that Venezuela would increase its foreign reserves by about $1.6 billion this year.
The official said that those reserves now topped $12 billion, up from around $10 billion before they clinched the IMF loan.
Venezuela received the $500 million first tranche of the IMF loan in July.
